events.event_label: dsRNA reduces or impairs transmission and virus transmission under Controlled Conditions
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p043.s009: Interestingly, there was no transmission of ChiLCV when B. tabaci was exposed to 3.0 μg/mL hsp70 dsRNA. PMC8909865.p043.s010: All the inoculated plants were without any leaf curl symptoms (Figure 3f) and tested ChiLCV-free in PCR at 35 days post-inoculation. PMC8909865.p043.s011: Probably virus transmission by B. tabaci completely inhibited at a higher concentration of hsp70 dsRNA.

events.event_label: virus titer and transmission affects leaf curl symptoms
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p046.s003: The melt curve of ChiLCV amplicon in qPCR produced specific peaks without any secondary peaks that confirmed the specificity of the reactions (Figure 4e). PMC8909865.p046.s004: When a portion of the same B. tabaci population was used for inoculation of ChiLCV in healthy chilli plants, a 75% decrease in transmission efficiency was confirmed in PCR test (Figure 4f) with no visible symptoms in the inoculated plants up to 50 days post-inoculation (Figure 4g). PMC8909865.p046.s005: Probably, the virus titer was too low in inoculated plants to produce strong visible symptoms, whereas 100% transmission and severe leaf curl symptoms were noted in plants inoculated by unexposed B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p046.s006: No transmission of ChiLCV was recorded in the plants mock-inoculated with untreated virus-free B. tabaci.

events.event_label: Hsp70 and fas2 affects B. tabaci
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p052.s001: Hsp70 and fas2 were found to be significantly upregulated in viruliferous B. tabaci along with several other genes. PMC8909865.p052.s002: Gene regulatory networking showed these genes were enriched with higher degrees of interactions. PMC8909865.p052.s003: Hsp70 transcripts increased upon ingestion of tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) and squash leaf curl virus (SLCV) in DNA microarray. PMC8909865.p052.s004: The role of hsp70 in begomovirus transmission is well studied.

events.event_label: hsp70 and fas2 is involved with siRNA
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p052.s009: Conserved 128 and 150 nt stretches in the hsp70 and fas2 genes, respectively, were found to be specific to B. tabaci without any cross-reactivity to humans, mice, birds, butterflies, bees, ants, and plants. PMC8909865.p052.s010: Each produced a putative siRNA of 21 nt. PMC8909865.p052.s011: dsRNA was synthesized by in vivo transcription to harvest large quantities of dsRNA at a low cost. PMC8909865.p052.s012: Bacterially expressed dsRNA is economical and convenient, as reported in several studies. PMC8909865.p052.s013: Before evaluating the efficacy of topically sprayed dsRNA, we tested it under controlled laboratory conditions.

events.event_label: dsRNA represses or inhibits hsp70 and fas2 under artificial diet
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p052.s018: Similarly, fas2 dsRNA at 3.0 μg/mL caused 72% mortality of B. tabaci 24 h post-feeding. PMC8909865.p052.s019: The dsRNA exposure downregulated the hsp70 and fas2 mRNA expressions by 12.85- and 8.53-fold, respectively. PMC8909865.p052.s020: The expression of an endogenous control gene was unregulated post-dsRNA exposure. PMC8909865.p052.s021: This indicated the specificity of the dsRNA constructs to target genes. PMC8909865.p052.s022: Hsp belongs to the multifunctional molecular chaperone family involved in the aggregation of damaged proteins, transportation, assembly, and disassembly of multi-structured units under stressed conditions.

events.event_label: fas2 affects MAPK and calcium levels
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p052.s024: In Drosophila melanogaster, Fas2 is involved in synaptic development and growth. PMC8909865.p052.s025: It is also known to function in intracellular signaling pathways that involve mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and regulate intracellular calcium levels. PMC8909865.p052.s026: However, the function of fas2 in B. tabaci is uncharacterized. PMC8909865.p052.s027: Kanakala et al. reported twisting of wings in B. tabaci upon silencing hsp70. PMC8909865.p052.s028: However, we did not record any morphological deformities in treated B. tabaci.

events.event_label: anti-Hsp70 antibody enhances or improves transmission
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p053.s009: The TYLCV titer decreased in B. tabaci Middle East Asia Minor 1 (MEAM 1) after feeding on hsp70 dsRNA-expressing tomato plants. PMC8909865.p053.s010: Transmission of TYLCV also dropped by 12% post-silencing of hsp70. PMC8909865.p053.s011: In the present study, the inability of B. tabaci Asia II 1 to retain and transmit ChiLCV post-silencing of hsp70 indicates that it might also play an important function in ChiLCV infection. PMC8909865.p053.s012: However, Gotz et al. reported an increase in TYLCV transmission upon blocking Hsp70 by anti-Hsp70 antibody in B. tabaci MEAM1. PMC8909865.p053.s013: It was hypothesized that the Hsp70-TYLCV interaction mediates the degradation of virions. PMC8909865.p053.s014: Downregulation of hsp70, hsp40, and hsp20 resulted in 3.1-, 1.5-, and 1.2-fold increases in cotton leaf curl virus (CLCuV) titer within B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p053.s015: Significantly increased transmission efficiency of CLCuV was noted in B. tabaci Asia II 1 when hsp70 was silenced. PMC8909865.p053.s016: The difference may be due to the variation in virus species and B. tabaci cryptic species.

PMC8909865.p053.s015: Significantly increased transmission efficiency of CLCuV was noted in B. tabaci Asia II 1 when hsp70 was silenced. PMC8909865.p053.s016: The difference may be due to the variation in virus species and B. tabaci cryptic species. PMC8909865.p053.s017: The interactions of B. tabaci with begomoviruses are not conserved and alter with cryptic species of B. tabaci and begomovirus species. PMC8909865.p053.s018: B. tabaci MEAM1 has two genes (Bta03000 and Bta02903) annotated as hsp70, and their amino acid sequences differ by 97.55%. PMC8909865.p053.s019: They might also exhibit differential responses to begomovirus infection.

events.event_label: dsRNA affects B. tabaci and transmission under artificial diet
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p054.s003: The naked dsRNA quickly degrades in higher temperatures and UV radiation under natural environmental conditions. PMC8909865.p054.s004: Besides, several insect species, mainly lepidopteran insects, have been observed to be refractory to RNAi due to degradation and poor intracellular transport of exogenous dsRNA. PMC8909865.p054.s005: Nucleases are the major factors limiting the efficacy of dsRNA. PMC8909865.p054.s006: In the first phase of the study, hsp70 dsRNA showed high potential in eradicating B. tabaci and inhibiting ChiLCV transmission. PMC8909865.p054.s007: In the next phase, the dsRNA construct was assessed under natural environmental conditions by spraying like an insecticide.

events.event_label: dsRNA affects transmission and B. tabaci under semi-field conditions
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p054.s009: Hence, naked hsp70 dsRNA without any delivery agent was topically sprayed onto the foliage of the ChiLCV-infected chilli plant under contained semi-field conditions. PMC8909865.p054.s010: B. tabaci adults were released on the dsRNA-sprayed plants to evaluate the dsRNA’s efficacy in eradicating B. tabaci and inhibiting the transmission of ChiLCV. PMC8909865.p054.s011: Considering the extracellular degradation of dsRNA and delivery through the host plant, a 10-fold higher dose than the controlled assay was used for topical application. PMC8909865.p054.s012: A 67.77% mortality with a 4.6-fold decrease in hsp70 mRNA levels in B. tabaci exposed to the dsRNA-sprayed plants was noted after 24 h of release. PMC8909865.p054.s013: Further, 1.84 × 108-fold decreased ChiLCV copies and 75% reduced transmission of ChiLCV indicated the efficiency of topically sprayed hsp70 dsRNA in managing both the virus and its vector.

events.event_label: dsRNA affects ChiLCV and B. tabaci under semi-field conditions
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p057.s001: In conclusion, the spray-on application of naked dsRNA targeting hsp70 of B. tabaci provides resistance to both ChiLCV and its vector, B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p057.s002: This is a novel alternative to hazardous insecticides and may be further assessed on a large scale for its efficacy under real-field conditions.

events.event_label: field conditions reduces or impairs RNAi and dsRNA
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p006.s001: Although several potential RNAi targets were identified for insects, including B. tabaci, most of those studies were conducted under controlled experimental conditions, and their efficacy under field conditions is limited. PMC8909865.p006.s002: Rapid degradation of dsRNA in the extracellular environment and lack of reliable dsRNA delivery technique limits its applicability under field conditions. PMC8909865.p006.s003: The objective of the present study was to induce resistance against B. tabaci and ChiLCV by spray-on application of dsRNA. PMC8909865.p006.s004: In the present study, B. tabaci hsp70 and fas2 were silenced and resultant effects in mortality and virus transmission were reported.

events.event_label: mtCOI gene affects B. tabaci and B. tabaci Asia II 1
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p034.s001: A homogeneous population of B. tabaci developed from a single adult female was characterized by sequencing the mtCOI gene. PMC8909865.p034.s002: PCR amplification of B. tabaci mtCOI with C1-J-2195 and L2-N-3014 primers (Table 1) showed an expected amplicon of ~860 bp on an agarose gel. PMC8909865.p034.s003: The nucleotide (nt) sequence showed 99.99% homology in BLASTn analysis with other B. tabaci Asia II 1 sequences in NCBI. PMC8909865.p034.s004: The sequence can be retrieved using the GenBank Accession No. MT920041.

events.event_label: hsp70 and fas2 is involved with siRNA
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p037.s001: A conserved 128 nt-long (2416 to 2543 nt) fragment of the hsp70 gene (~2.5 kb) and a 150 nt-long (1085 to 1234 nt) fragment of the fas2 gene (~1.4 kb) of B. tabaci were selected for dsRNA designing (Figure 1a,b). PMC8909865.p037.s002: In siRNA Wizard 3.1, the 128 nt-long B. tabaci hsp70 fragment produced a putative siRNA of 21 nt (5’-GAUCCAUCCAUGCCGUUAAUC-3’). PMC8909865.p037.s003: The 150 nt-long fas2 fragment also yielded one putative siRNA of 21 nt (5’-GGACGGAAGAAGGCAUAAUCA-3’). PMC8909865.p037.s004: The dsRNA sequence was specific to B. tabaci, and no cross-reactivity was recorded with other organisms such as Homo sapiens, Mus musculus, Aves (taxid:8782), Lepidoptera (taxid:7088), Hymenoptera (taxid:7399), Formicidae (taxid:36668), and plants (taxid:3193) in BLAST analysis.

events.event_label: dsRNA and Oral delivery affects mortality
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p039.s003: Mortality of 67.77% of B. tabaci was observed at 24 h upon feeding on 1.0 μg/mL hsp70 dsRNA. PMC8909865.p039.s004: The mortality of B. tabaci significantly increased with an increase in dsRNA concentration. PMC8909865.p039.s005: The mean mortality was 70.0% when hsp70 dsRNA was fed to B. tabaci adults at 2.0 μg/mL, and it increased significantly up to 82.22% at 3.0 μg/mL hsp70 dsRNA (Figure 2b). PMC8909865.p039.s006: Oral delivery of fas2 dsRNA at 1.0 μg/mL exhibited 39.33% mean mortality after 24 h (Figure 2b). PMC8909865.p039.s007: Significantly higher mortality (62 and 72%) of B. tabaci adults was recorded when 2.0 and 3.0 μg/mL fas2 dsRNA was orally delivered to B. tabaci under controlled laboratory conditions.

events.event_label: feeding and dsRNA affects hsp70 mRNA expression
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p040.s001: RT-qPCR analysis showed that hsp70 dsRNA significantly reduced the hsp70 mRNA expression levels in treated B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p040.s002: Hsp70 mRNA levels in adult B. tabaci were decreased by 5.43-fold with respect to an endogenous control gene, β-actin, post-24 h feeding on hsp70 dsRNA (Figure 2c). PMC8909865.p040.s003: The mRNA expression levels were significantly reduced with an increase in hsp70 dsRNA concentration. PMC8909865.p040.s004: An exposure to hsp70 dsRNA at 2.0 μg/mL for 24 h significantly reduced the hsp70 mRNA expression by 11.32-fold and up to 12.85-fold when fed with 3.0 μg/mL hsp70 dsRNA.

PMC8909865.p159.s006: A single specific peak at 81 °C indicates the specificity of the reactions. PMC8909865.p159.s008: (d) Mean ChiLCV copy numbers retained by fas2 dsRNA-treated B. tabaci after 24 h of acquisition feeding on ChiLCV-infected plants. PMC8909865.p159.s009: The error bars are standard error of the mean (SEM). PMC8909865.p159.s010: Mean denoted by an asterisk (*) indicates a significant difference (p < 0.05).

events.event_label: Hsp, cyclophilins, peptidoglycan recognition protein, and midgut protein affects CP
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p005.s015: Interrupting the interrelationship between B. tabaci and begomovirus using RNAi is a promising approach.. For successful persistent-circulative transmission, the begomovirus particles need to cross the midgut barrier of B. tabaci to circulate in hemolymph and reach the primary salivary glands. PMC8909865.p005.s016: Several proteins at the midguts of B. tabaci, such as heat shock proteins (Hsp), cyclophilins, peptidoglycan recognition protein, and a midgut protein, are known to interact with begomovirus coat protein (CP) for successful internalization. PMC8909865.p005.s017: RNA-Seq of B. tabaci in response to begomoviruses revealed significant upregulations of hsp70, fasciclin 2 (fas2), and several other transcripts. PMC8909865.p005.s018: In gene regulatory network analyses, these genes were enriched with higher degrees of interactions. PMC8909865.p005.s019: The same trend was recorded in the mRNA expression in reverse transcriptase quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) post-exposure to ChiLCV.

events.event_label: dsRNA affects mortality, Transmission, and B. tabaci
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p002.s001: Chilli leaf curl virus (ChiLCV; genus: Begomovirus), transmitted by Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) in a persistent-circulative manner, is a major constraint in chilli production. PMC8909865.p002.s002: The present study demonstrates for the first time that a topical spray of naked double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) on chilli plants causes mortality and inability to acquire and transmit ChiLCV in B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p002.s003: dsRNA targeting heat shock protein 70 (hsp70) and fasciclin 2 (fas2) of B. tabaci Asia II 1 was first assessed under controlled conditions through oral delivery. PMC8909865.p002.s004: Hsp70 and fas2 dsRNA resulted in up to 82.22% and 72% mortality of B. tabaci and around 12.4- and 8.5-fold decreases in mRNA levels, respectively, 24 h post-ingestion. PMC8909865.p002.s006: However, ChiLCV copies significantly increased in fas2 dsRNA-fed B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p002.s007: Transmission of ChiLCV by B. tabaci was completely inhibited post-24 h feeding on hsp70 dsRNA at 3 μg/mL. Naked hsp70 dsRNA was topically sprayed on ChiLCV-infected chilli plants like an insecticide. PMC8909865.p002.s008: 67.77% mortality of B. tabaci, 4.6-fold downregulation of hsp70 mRNA, and 1.34 × 1015-fold decreased ChiLCV copies in B. tabaci were recorded when adults were exposed to the dsRNA-treated plants under semi-field conditions. PMC8909865.p002.s009: Foliar application of naked dsRNA reduced the ChiLCV transmission by 75% without any visible symptoms in the inoculated plants. PMC8909865.p002.s010: A total of 2 consecutive sprays of dsRNA provided significant protection to B. tabaci for up to 20 days under semi-field conditions.

events.event_label: cyclophilins and midgut protein affects CP
events.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p005.s015: Interrupting the interrelationship between B. tabaci and begomovirus using RNAi is a promising approach.. For successful persistent-circulative transmission, the begomovirus particles need to cross the midgut barrier of B. tabaci to circulate in hemolymph and reach the primary salivary glands. PMC8909865.p005.s016: Several proteins at the midguts of B. tabaci, such as heat shock proteins (Hsp), cyclophilins, peptidoglycan recognition protein, and a midgut protein, are known to interact with begomovirus coat protein (CP) for successful internalization. PMC8909865.p005.s017: RNA-Seq of B. tabaci in response to begomoviruses revealed significant upregulations of hsp70, fasciclin 2 (fas2), and several other transcripts. PMC8909865.p005.s018: In gene regulatory network analyses, these genes were enriched with higher degrees of interactions. PMC8909865.p005.s019: The same trend was recorded in the mRNA expression in reverse transcriptase quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) post-exposure to ChiLCV.

PMC8909865.p045.s006: A 67.77% mortality of adult B. tabaci was recorded post-24 h exposure to dsRNA-treated plants (Figure 4a). PMC8909865.p049.s008: Significantly higher mortality was sustained up to 8 days after the second application and thereafter started decreasing. PMC8909865.p051.s001: Several management strategies have been adopted around the world, with insecticides as the core component for the management of the B. tabaci-ChiLCV complex. PMC8909865.p051.s002: However, the use of chemical insecticides has led to several detrimental effects like the development of insecticide-resistant B. tabaci population, destruction of beneficial organisms, environmental contamination, and health hazards. PMC8909865.p051.s003: There is a need for an alternative eco-friendly approach in managing B. tabaci-ChiLCV. PMC8909865.p051.s004: RNAi or post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) was introduced to study the functionality of specific genes through knocking down target gene mRNA.

PMC8909865.p051.s009: RNAi using dsRNA constructs is not suitable for field conditions due to rapid degradation and a lack of reliable delivery agents. PMC8909865.p051.s010: In the present study, for the first time, we demonstrated the efficacy of a naked dsRNA against an insect pest by spray-on application under semi-field conditions. PMC8909865.p051.s011: The dsRNA construct targeting the hsp70 gene of B. tabaci not only induced mortality in B. tabaci but also inhibited the transmission of ChiLCV from infected to healthy chilli plants by B. tabaci.

PMC8909865.p054.s001: Although RNAi has emerged as a promising alternative to suppress crop pests, there are limitations in the application of dsRNA as a ‘spray-on’ technology for field use. PMC8909865.p054.s002: Reduced stability in the extracellular environments of dsRNA contributes to poor RNAi response. PMC8909865.p054.s003: The naked dsRNA quickly degrades in higher temperatures and UV radiation under natural environmental conditions. PMC8909865.p054.s004: Besides, several insect species, mainly lepidopteran insects, have been observed to be refractory to RNAi due to degradation and poor intracellular transport of exogenous dsRNA.

PMC8909865.p054.s012: A 67.77% mortality with a 4.6-fold decrease in hsp70 mRNA levels in B. tabaci exposed to the dsRNA-sprayed plants was noted after 24 h of release. PMC8909865.p054.s013: Further, 1.84 × 108-fold decreased ChiLCV copies and 75% reduced transmission of ChiLCV indicated the efficiency of topically sprayed hsp70 dsRNA in managing both the virus and its vector.

PMC8909865.p055.s001: Topical application of dsRNA could provide resistance for 12 to 21 days against plant viruses. PMC8909865.p055.s002: In the present study, dsRNA was detected in the leaf tissues up to 6 h post-application. PMC8909865.p055.s003: Significant mortality of B. tabaci on the treated plants persisted up to 8 days and was further sustained up to 20 days with a second spray on the 10th day. PMC8909865.p055.s004: Protection of the plants during the early growth stage is crucial in the management of begomoviruses.

relations.evidence_context_text: PMC8909865.p002.s001: Chilli leaf curl virus (ChiLCV; genus: Begomovirus), transmitted by Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) in a persistent-circulative manner, is a major constraint in chilli production. PMC8909865.p002.s002: The present study demonstrates for the first time that a topical spray of naked double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) on chilli plants causes mortality and inability to acquire and transmit ChiLCV in B. tabaci. PMC8909865.p039.s005: The mean mortality was 70.0% when hsp70 dsRNA was fed to B. tabaci adults at 2.0 μg/mL, and it increased significantly up to 82.22% at 3.0 μg/mL hsp70 dsRNA (Figure 2b). PMC8909865.p039.s006: Oral delivery of fas2 dsRNA at 1.0 μg/mL exhibited 39.33% mean mortality after 24 h (Figure 2b). PMC8909865.p039.s007: Significantly higher mortality (62 and 72%) of B. tabaci adults was recorded when 2.0 and 3.0 μg/mL fas2 dsRNA was orally delivered to B. tabaci under controlled laboratory conditions.

relations.subject: insecticides

evidence.text: Several management strategies have been adopted around the world, with insecticides as the core component for the management of the B. tabaci-ChiLCV complex.

However, the use of chemical insecticides has led to several detrimental effects like the development of insecticide-resistant B. tabaci population, destruction of beneficial organisms, environmental contamination, and health hazards.

Chilli leaf curl virus (ChiLCV; genus: Begomovirus), transmitted by Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius) (Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae) in a persistent-circulative manner, is a major constraint in chilli production.
The present study demonstrates for the first time that a topical spray of naked double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) on chilli plants causes mortality and inability to acquire and transmit ChiLCV in B.

Silverleaf whitefly [Bemisia tabaci (Gennadius), Hemiptera: Aleyrodidae] is a phloem-feeding hemipteran insect that has been reported to infest over 600 plant species worldwide.

Although RNAi has emerged as a promising alternative to suppress crop pests, there are limitations in the application of dsRNA as a ‘spray-on’ technology for field use.
Reduced stability in the extracellular environments of dsRNA contributes to poor RNAi response.
The naked dsRNA quickly degrades in higher temperatures and UV radiation under natural environmental conditions.
Besides, several insect species, mainly lepidopteran insects, have been observed to be refractory to RNAi due to degradation and poor intracellular transport of exogenous dsRNA.
Nucleases are the major factors limiting the efficacy of dsRNA.
